test_policy.notes: "Submitting SAT and ACT test scores is optional; students who choose not to submit their scores are at no disadvantage." Applicants say on the application whether they want scores considered; self-reported scores are accepted and both tests are superscored; admitted students who had scores considered must send official scores. Score-reporting codes: SAT 2086, ACT 2702. Common App grid: tests never required.

requirements.notes: Common App, Coalition (Scoir) or QuestBridge application, which includes a personal statement; the page describes no separate supplemental essay prompt, so that field is left blank. Two recommendations from core academic teachers (10th-12th grade), a counselor recommendation, an official transcript, and mid-year grades by February 15 (not required by the ED I deadline); ED applicants also submit the signed Early Decision Agreement. The $60 fee is waived for non-U.S. citizens (not dual citizens or permanent residents) and for students with fee waivers. The page describes no admissions interview; international applicants are encouraged to submit InitialView or Vericant videos before the deadline. Optional: arts portfolio (SlideRoom, $12), digital presence, Glimpse video (domestic), VIVA research video. Aid applicants must submit the CSS Profile (international students pay no extra form; no PDF or paper copies).

deadlines.label: Early Decision I
deadlines.notes: Binding. Notification "Mid-December" (no exact date published). The page gives no year; the Common App 2026-27 grid also lists 11/01/2026. International applicants have the same deadlines.

deadlines.label: Regular Decision
deadlines.notes: Notification "Late March" (no exact date published). Mid-year grades due February 15.

deadlines.label: Financial aid (ED I)
deadlines.notes: CSS Profile submission (opens October 1); aid is requested on the admission application.

deadlines.label: Financial aid (ED II)
deadlines.notes: CSS Profile submission. The international-applicants page says the CSS fee-waiver request deadline is January 22 for ED II and RD, while the aid page says it is the application deadline; use January 15.

deadlines.label: Financial aid (RD)
deadlines.notes: CSS Profile submission, same date as the application deadline.

english_policy.waiver_notes: Required of non-native English speakers who do not study at a secondary school where English is the primary language of instruction: TOEFL iBT, IELTS or Duolingo English Test. Colgate does not waive the requirement based on SAT results. Scores must come from the official testing agency (TOEFL code 2086).

english.notes: The page lists "TOEFL IBT (Test of English as a Foreign Language) = 4.5" without naming the scale; 4.5 can only be on the new 1-6 scale, so it is entered here. No 0-120 minimum is published.

aid.notes: Colgate "meets 100% of demonstrated financial need for every admitted student" and states "Need-aware admissions: We consider financial need during the review process for all applicants. However, our most competitive applicants are admitted regardless of whether they have applied for financial aid." Aid is need-based only; the university "does not offer academic merit scholarships" (the CDS H6 box for non-need-based aid to nonresidents is ticked, but H1 shows only $218,715 of non-need institutional aid in total). International students must request aid on the application and submit the CSS Profile (code 2086) by the application deadline; CSS fee waivers are available through the applicant portal. International students who do not apply for or qualify for aid at admission are not eligible later; no annual reapplication. CDS H6: 119 degree-seeking nonresidents received institutional aid, average $86,649.

cost.notes: Colgate's 2026-27 first-year on-campus figures: tuition $76,828, Student Activity Fee $462, housing $9,348 + food $10,008 (room_board shown = their sum), books $1,600; the page's total estimated cost of attendance is $100,224. Other shown = non-billed costs $3,578 minus books: transportation $800+ (base amount, varies with home address), personal $1,128, average loan fees $50. Student health insurance ($1,805) is extra unless waived. The 2025-26 CDS G1 lists older figures (tuition $73,206, fees $440, food and housing $18,446), so the website values are used. Institutional aid for nonresidents (CDS H6): 119 students, average $86,649.

ielts.note: No code published; scores must be sent by the testing agency.

duolingo.note: No code published; scores must be sent by the testing agency (Duolingo).

tier_notes.computer_science: Small liberal-arts CS program (7.91% of 2024-25 degrees, CDS J1).
tier_notes.biology_life_sci: Biology is a big major (13.65% of degrees, CDS J1) but a small, undergraduate-only department.
tier_notes.pre_med: Pre-health advising at a liberal-arts college; no standout national rank.
tier_notes.economics: Social sciences are about a third of degrees (31.95%, CDS J1); economics sits in that group; a strong liberal-arts program but not a top-10 one (editorial judgment).
tier_notes.math_physics: Math/statistics 2.37% and physical sciences 4.15% of degrees (CDS J1): small departments.
tier_notes.humanities: Solid liberal-arts humanities and a required core curriculum (English 3.86%, history 3.36%, CDS J1), no national top-15 program.
tier_notes.arts_design: Visual and performing arts are 3.86% of degrees (CDS J1); no design-school depth.
tier_notes.engineering: No engineering major (CDS J1 reports no engineering degrees).
tier_notes.business: No business major (CDS J1 reports no business degrees).
tier_notes.nursing: No nursing program (CDS J1 reports no health-professions degrees).
